rows.title: A year after Colorado exempted menstrual products and diapers from state sales tax, few local governments have followed suit
rows.standfirst: The state sales tax makes up just a fraction of what consumers pay. Denver, Aurora and Boulder have removed local taxes on the hygiene products, but Colorado Springs and other Front Range cities have not.

rows.title: Colorado backcountry off-roading program puts disabled adventurers on the throttle
rows.standfirst: Return to Dirt lets people with spinal cord injuries take the wheel in specially equipped off-road rigs that can be driven with adaptive controls.

rows.title: Xcel must cut emissions from its gas business 22% by 2030. The role heat pumps can play is a point of dispute.
rows.standfirst: Environmental groups say heat pumps can get most of the emissions out. Xcel paid for a study that begs to differ.

rows.title: Deaths of people who are homeless in Denver surge 50% since last year
rows.standfirst: Coroner blames “tightening grip of fentanyl” for the rising deaths, hitting 166 people so far this year, compared with 108 last year

rows.title: One-fifth of Crested Butte’s restaurants have closed, leaving tourists hungry
rows.standfirst: To top it off, the grocery store will be temporarily closing soon. But thankfully, this is a short-term problem.

rows.title: What’s Working: What would you do with $10,000? A new Denver venture firm wants to know.
rows.standfirst: With venture funding on the decline, “pre-founding” startup capital emerges to reward ideas. Plus: Denver’s venture industry declining less than other cities, rising minimum wages and more

rows.title: Colorado’s sports betting tax revenue doubled, meaning millions more for water projects
rows.standfirst: The big increase was expected after the legislature passed a bill in 2022 limiting the number of free bets that sports betting operators could offer starting Jan. 1, 2023

rows.title: Early closure of Pueblo coal plant could force Xcel customers to pay up to $89M for water it doesn’t need
rows.standfirst: Customers of the state’s largest utility also are responsible for debt service on $27 million spent on never used southeastern Colorado ditch rights

rows.title: Colorado’s biggest buildings clash with air regulators over coming greenhouse gas rules
rows.standfirst: State regulators will vote this month on demanding emissions savings from landlords as the next key step in the climate change battle.

rows.title: Father sues Lafayette for not providing indoor shelter for homeless people like him and his son
rows.standfirst: Civil rights lawyers say a critical mass of claims filed in Colorado cities could force a decision about whether homeless people can be moved from campsites when no other shelter exists

rows.title: Colorado cities with residential growth caps start to contend with new state law banning the limits
rows.standfirst: Lakewood voted to adhere to the law by repealing its municipal cap. Boulder is set to repeal its cap, too. Golden and Lafayette have so far punted.

rows.title: For women farm owners in Colorado, the leading concerns are crops and animals, not sexism
rows.standfirst: More women are finding training and support for dealing with pests, weather and how to purchase land to farm and ranch in Colorado

rows.title: What’s Working: Denver had the second highest annual inflation rate in the U.S. last month
rows.standfirst: Inflation is slowing and economists are hopeful rates will decline further in 2024. Plus: Blame higher energy and housing costs, Colorado job growth, startups set a record and more!

rows.title: As some Colorado drive-ins fade out, others keep the dream alive
rows.standfirst: Even as the 88 Drive-In in Commerce City gets ready to close, remaining drive-in theater owners around Colorado are still hopeful

rows.title: HOA-foreclosed homes in Colorado are auctioned off for a fraction of their market value, erasing years of equity
rows.standfirst: A Colorado Sun investigation found that more than 250 HOA-foreclosed properties have been auctioned off in the state since 2018. At least 100 of them were sold for $60,000 or less.

rows.title: Want a hot tub at your Colorado ski town home? You might have to offset its emissions first.
rows.standfirst: Breckenridge — and soon Summit County — is adopting a “renewable energy mitigation plan” to offset greenhouse gases from outdoor amenities

rows.title: 95 oil and gas wells are in the way of economic development in Frederick. Town officials want the barrier gone.
rows.standfirst: Frederick, and its neighbor Dacono, are appealing to state regulators to force K.P. Kauffman to plug and abandon wells developers say are making them look elsewhere.

rows.title: Why a Colorado mattress recycler sends old mattresses to the landfill
rows.standfirst: Spring Back Colorado, the Commerce City nonprofit, is desperately trying to figure out how to recycle pocket-coil mattresses affordably. It’s a challenge for the entire industry, even in states with mattress recycling laws.

rows.title: Jared Polis, Democratic state lawmakers call for more changes to Colorado’s HOA laws after Colorado Sun investigation
rows.standfirst: The Sun’s investigation, published this week, found that HOAs have filed roughly 3,000 foreclosure cases since 2018, more than 250 of which have resulted in properties being auctioned off. At least 100 of the properties auctioned off were sold for $60,000 or less, according to court records.

rows.title: King Soopers closure highlights challenge of getting healthy food in southeastern Colorado Springs
rows.standfirst: Colorado Springs residents are sounding the alarm as they wait for the grocer to reopen this fall

rows.title: Xcel will raise electric bills again next month. A quarter of the hike will cover closing coal-fired power plants.
rows.standfirst: The utility’s 1.6 million Colorado customers will see their bills rise 4.4% — about $4 on the average residential bill — on Sept. 1

rows.title: More than 100 Summit County homeowners sue over crackdown on short-term rentals
rows.standfirst: The lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court seeks to overturn “misguided and unlawful” regulations. “We want to make Summit County ground zero for this fight.”

rows.title: What happened to Centura Health? Why the Colorado hospital brand name is about to disappear.
rows.standfirst: CommonSpirit Health and AdventHealth, the two systems that partnered to form Centura, are splitting up

rows.title: Federal appeals court derails Uinta Basin Railway plan to send billions more gallons of Utah crude through Colorado
rows.standfirst: The decision directs the Surface Transportation Board to redo its review and consider potential threats the railway poses to the Colorado River and communities far down the line

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado has 190,000 job openings and 95,000 unemployed people — a disconnect?
rows.standfirst: QUICK LINKS: What else the labor data says | The 190,000 job openings | State unemployment rates | The poll: Working or not? | $1 million cybersecurity grant Colorado seems to be in a bit of a standstill when it comes to jobs. Job growth in July was flat. The higher unemployment rate, an increase […]

rows.title: Is LoDo still thriving? Here’s how Coors Field helped shape a developing Denver neighborhood.
rows.standfirst: Investors, including the Monfort family, now are looking for opportunities in the blocks beyond the Ballpark neighborhood

rows.title: The giant troll in Victor: A Danish artist brings one of his international sculptures to an old Colorado mining town
rows.standfirst: The Gold Camp District Impact Group brought in Thomas Dambo’s “Rita the Rock Planter” as it tries to bring together the community and spark the local economy

rows.title: Colorado governor orders his administration to rework its housing initiatives after the legislature killed his signature bill
rows.standfirst: The decree will have limited effect, but it’s a strong signal to local governments and state lawmakers that Jared Polis is unwilling to back down on his affordable housing push

rows.title: Manager at one of Colorado’s largest cannabis businesses is tapped to lead New Mexico’s team of marijuana regulators
rows.standfirst: Todd Stevens most recently served as the manager of training and development at Native Roots Cannabis Co.

rows.title: BLM shifts green on 2 million Western Slope acres, setting up Colorado clash of environment vs. oil
rows.standfirst: Far bigger chunks of pristine public lands would be walled off from extraction, as federal land managers are ordered to consider climate impacts of activities on land spanning Eagle, Mesa and Pitkin counties

rows.title: Broncos unveil $100M upgrade to Empower Field at Mile High featuring mammoth scoreboard
rows.standfirst: The team showed off the new scoreboard Friday, a day before the Broncos play their preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s 190,000 job openings
rows.standfirst: Where do those numbers come from? We found some, but here’s what else you need to know about job data.

rows.title: Tight rental market leaves some residents displaced by Gunnison trailer park redevelopment with no place to go
rows.standfirst: 50 people, half of them children, were given a month to leave the Frontier Land community so trailers could be scraped and replaced by higher priced new mobile homes

rows.title: Residential development in Erie, Longmont stalled after wells plugged decades ago start leaking oil and gas
rows.standfirst: One orphaned well was added to Colorado regulators’ long list of projects, and another may be joining it. Both may have to wait in line.

rows.title: Denverites are split on whether the Mile High City is headed in the right direction, according to a new poll
rows.standfirst: The survey, conducted jointly by a Democratic and Republican pollster, also found that Denver’s residents are most concerned with homelessness and the high cost of housing

rows.title: Colorado revives “cash for clunkers,” offers $6,000 for an old car you trade for an EV
rows.standfirst: Piling clunker credits on top of existing state and federal electric vehicle rebates can land you a very, very cheap new car.

rows.title: Are private transportation companies the answer to Colorado’s school bus driver shortage?
rows.standfirst: Students with disabilities, who are homeless or living in foster homes have the right to free transportation to their schools. School districts’ costs are rising.
